nodes.summary: If $A = (a_{ij})$ is a real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ symmetric Toeplitz matrix, with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$, then $a_{ij} = a_{ji}$ for all $i, j$.
nodes.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrices are symmetric

nodes.summary: Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be a real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$. If $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $c(-k) = c(k)$ for every integer $k$ and $a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$, then $A$ is a symmetric Toeplitz matrix.
nodes.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrices from even coefficients

nodes.summary: A real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$, with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$, is symmetric Toeplitz if there is a function $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $c(-k) = c(k)$ for every integer $k$ and $a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$.
nodes.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrix

nodes.summary: Let $A = (a_{ij})$ be a real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$. If $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfies $a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$, then $A$ is a Toeplitz matrix.
nodes.title: Toeplitz matrices from coefficients

nodes.summary: A real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix $A = (a_{ij})$, with rows and columns indexed by $\{0, \dots, n\}$, is Toeplitz if there is a function $c : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $a_{ij} = c(i - j)$ for all $i, j$. Equivalently, $A$ is constant along each of its diagonals.
nodes.title: Toeplitz matrix

nodes.summary: Every real $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ symmetric Toeplitz matrix is a Toeplitz matrix.
nodes.title: Symmetric Toeplitz matrices are Toeplitz

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a set with a zero element and $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $R$. For every natural number $i$, the $(i, i)$ entry of the lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $a_0$.
nodes.title: Diagonal entries of a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a set with a zero element and $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $R$. For natural numbers $i < j$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Entries above the diagonal of a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a set with a zero element and $a = (a_0, a_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $R$. For natural numbers $j \le i$, the $(i, j)$ entry of the lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is $a_{i-j}$.
nodes.title: Entries on and below the diagonal of a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a set with a zero element $0$ and let $a = (a_0, a_1, a_2, \dots)$ be a sequence in $R$. The lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix of $a$ is the matrix with rows and columns indexed by $\mathbb{N}$ whose $(i, j)$ entry is $a_{i-j}$ when $j \le i$ and $0$ when $j > i$. In particular it is constant along each diagonal and vanishes strictly above the main diagonal.
nodes.title: Lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
